stops.narrative: Inspect the miniature’s scale and visible forms. Then use the selected Vietnam map to compare a drum containing other bronze objects, a presumed burial association and later production evidence. Each record has its own place and date; none establishes this miniature’s workshop or purpose.

Find the roof, opening and raised platform using the modern notes. The catalogue proposes an incense-burner lid. Regional offerings and the excavated Huitzilapa tomb supply comparisons, while this model retains an unknown precise findspot and two published date ranges.

Compare the Mound City survey with its separately dated restored-site photograph. The existing North Fork Works plan represents Hopewell Mound Group, a different site. Construction evidence at Hopeton and named contemporary Miami voices add distinct kinds of knowledge without making the surveys ancient eyewitness views.

conclusion: A useful explanation connects a particular claim with the evidence that can test it. A visible roof supports observation; a documented deposit supplies an association; a survey records a landscape at a later time. Keep an object’s unknown history open, and identify the people and methods behind later interpretation and care.

evidence.prompt: Which claim is best supported by the supplied Colima evidence?

options.text: The photographed model has a roof and platform; the catalogue proposes that it may have been an incense-burner lid.
options.feedback: This distinguishes visible features from a qualified catalogue interpretation. Neither step supplies an exact tomb or an associated burner body.

options.text: Because another shaft tomb was excavated at Huitzilapa, this model came from that tomb.
options.feedback: A documented regional comparison does not transfer its findspot to a different object.

options.text: Similar model buildings demonstrate one government across western Mexico.
options.feedback: Shared forms can coexist with regional and political differences. A style is not a recovered constitution or boundary.
